entries.title: CTA janitor fatally stabbed during argument at CTA station on Near West Side
entries.summary: <p>A CTA janitor died after being stabbed during an argument at a CTA train station on the Near West Side Thursday afternoon, police said.</p><p>Julian Mobley, 41, was at the Damen Green Line CTA station in the 2000 block of West Lake Street around 3 p.m. when another man approached and began an argument, according to Chicago police and ATU Local 308, the union that represents CTA workers including Mobley. </p><p>The men began physically fighting and the suspect stabbed Mobley in the neck with a sharp object. He was taken to Stroger Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.</p><p>The suspect fled the scene heading west, police said. No one is in custody and detectives are investigating. Green Line trains were bypassing the Damen station as of around 6 p.m.</p><p>Mobley has been a member of Local 308 since 2018, according to union president Pennie McCoach. He was a father of two, a 14-year-old and an 18-month-old, and had been married to his wife for 20 years, she said.</p><p>Mobley was mild-mannered and kind, and his eyes lit up when he talked about his children, according to rail janitor and union board member Audrey Veasley.</p><p>"His character is, he was a gentleman," Veasley said during a news conference hours after the incident. "He was a real man."</p><p>McCoach said Mobley's death is another example of why more safety measures are needed for CTA workers and called for immediate action — such as a review of safety protocols, increased security and better training — from the transit authority. Mobley is the second CTA employee to be killed while on the job in the last several months. In June, CTA switchman Kevin Barlow was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/29/god-has-taken-his-angel-friends-and-family-mourn-cta-worker-fatally-shot-in-roseland" >shot and killed while on duty</a>.</p><p>"Let me be clear: This is not a tragedy, this is a safety failure," McCoach said. "Our members show up every single day to serve the people of Chicago. They keep this city moving. They deserve to return home safely. That is a basic right, not a privilege."</p><p>Crime on the CTA had <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/07/08/cta-transit-crime-security-surge" >reportedly dropped for six consecutive months</a> earlier this year following beefed-up security due to a high number of violent crimes. But McCoach questioned the numbers released by the transit authority.</p><p>"I don't truly believe in what they're giving us because every day my phone rings some type of way that one of our members has been assaulted or harmed, and these types of incidents occur," she said. "The numbers, I don't think they're valid. I think they're fictitious and they're not real."</p><p>The CTA didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.</p>

entries.title: White Sox repeating their Game 1 lineup in Thursday night showdown with Guardians ace Parker Messick
entries.summary: <p>In Thursday night's Game 4 of the American League Division Series against the Guardians, the White Sox will be playing in front of a capacity crowd with a chance to clinch a postseason series at home for the first time 120 years of franchise history. They're also coming off a 9-3 stinker effort in Game 3 where the offense struck out 19 times—an MLB postseason nine-inning record—and the pitching staff walked 10 batters.</p><p>"It was one of our highest chase rates of the year, and so I think we were a little sped up yesterday," said manager Will Venable of the offense. "We've talked about it all year, Friday nights at the Rate and how special they've been and how charged up they've been. It was different yesterday. I'm not sure that there was anything that myself or Sho or anybody else could have said to prepare them for that. They had to experience it for themselves."</p><p>To add to things, and reiterate the theme that postseason baseball is difficult and full of challenges, Guardians ace left-hander Parker Messick takes the mound in Game 4. Led by a Munetaka Murakami two-run blast, the White Sox were able to chase Messick after 4 1/3 innings in Game 1, having run him up to 87 pitches. But the Sox' typical lineup against left-handed starters usually excludes Sam Antonacci; a bright spot who reached base four times in Game 3.</p><p>Game 4 will offer no exception.<br></p><ol id="rte-6a525cf0-c362-11f1-9619-ff37ca6a3819" start="1"><li>Chase Meidroth, 2B (R)</li><li>Randal Grichuk, LF (R)</li><li>Miguel Vargas, 3B (R)</li><li>Munetaka Murakami, 1B (L)</li><li>Tommy Pham, DH (R)</li><li>Brenton Doyle, CF (R)</li><li>Kyle Teel, C (L)</li><li>Braden Montgomery, RF (S)</li><li>Colson Montgomery, SS (L)</li></ol><p>"We've seen [Messick] a lot," said outfielder Tristan Peters. "We know kind of how he's going to pitch us. Maybe he changes it up a little bit, but we know what he's got. I'm very confident in our guys that I think we'll hit him well."</p><p>Rookie left-hander Hagen Smith is opening for the White Sox in Game 4, which will be the first time the club's pitching depth will be tested by games on back-to-back games in the ALDS. Smith opening games has mostly gone great, but he walked a pair of batters in 2/3 of an inning while throwing 21 pitches in Game 3, so he's not a good bet to get more than six outs on Thursday night.</p><p>Even with Grant Taylor relatively rested and available for at least four outs, by Venable's description, the Sox are at a point where they will need bulk innings at some point from one of their traditional starters.</p><p>"[Erick] Fedde is a guy who will be part of that; [Anthony] Kay, although we've been using him in shorter stints and more frequently, will be part of it as well," Venable said. "In those middle innings, those are two names that you'll likely see."</p><p>Fedde, despite being a right-hander who makes his living throwing lots of sweeping sliders, actually fared better against left-handers (.699 OPS) this season. He'll need that to hold true against a Guardians order filled to the brim with left-handers.<br></p><ol id="rte-6a525cf1-c362-11f1-9619-ff37ca6a3819" start="1"><li>Steven Kwan, CF (L)</li><li>Jose Ramirez, 3B (S)</li><li>Chase DeLauter, RF (L)</li><li>Jo Adell, DH (R)</li><li>Nathaniel Lowe, 1B (L)</li><li>Angel Martinez, LF (S)</li><li>Travis Bazzana, 2B (L)</li><li>Austin Hedges, CF (R)</li><li>Brayan Rocchio, SS (S)</li></ol><p>If the Sox win, they'll be popping champagne in their home clubhouse and enjoying three days off before the ALCS begins on Monday. If they lose, they'll be packing their bags for a climactic Game 5 in Cleveland on Saturday.</p>
entries.author: James Fegan
